content:
A payment batch contains separate payment_batch_items. Their principal, obligation reference, recipient version and intended bank reference are distinct from a submission attempt. A bank acknowledgement may be pending even though a payment was committed. ACK_PENDING does not establish either failure or success. A trace of a submission_attempt produces a bank_receipts record after trace_delay. A settled bank receipt is authoritative; a portal summary is not.

propose_batch_item_payment submits exactly the item's principal and its explicitly selected bank_version. submission_key is scoped to the batch item. Repeating the same key and the same parameters returns the original attempt without another debit. The same key with different parameters is rejected. A new key creates a new submission, including when another key already produced payment; callers are responsible for avoiding duplicate business payment. The submitted recipient must be current at transmission; a later recipient edit does not change an already sent instruction.

A bank may reject an unrecognized account version without debiting funds. Only an actual rejection or bank-confirmed NOT_RECEIVED establishes that attempt did not pay. An item in an outdated batch file can be VOID even if a draft attempt exists. A currently verified but economically wrong bank reference can receive a legal payment. Customer intent and actual obligation state must also be checked. A recipient change requires approved bank evidence for that item; it does not prove a prior attempt was cancelled.

The instruction amount on a submission attempt is its nominal principal. A final SETTLED bank receipt can report a smaller accepted amount; this is final settlement of that accepted portion, not confirmation that the whole invoice was paid. A zero accepted amount is NOT_RECEIVED. A trace reports both amount_minor (actually accepted) and instruction_minor (nominal). Several receipts for one attempt are observations of the same payment, not additional money. A portion rejected before acceptance is not a future expected receipt. Starting account balances already reconcile these historical acceptances.

propose_batch_residual_payment submits a chosen amount_minor, positive and no greater than the item's original principal. It otherwise uses the same bank-version and item-scoped idempotency rules as propose_batch_item_payment. Both interfaces can create an additional payment with a new key; neither computes the supplier's remaining economic obligation. The whole-item interface continues to transmit the whole principal.

## Exact service interfaces

- Use `propose_batch_recipient_update(item_id, submission_id)` to prepare the recipient-version repair for one batch item after the required evidence has actually been uploaded.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_attempt_trace`

Request the bank receipt for a submission attempt whose acknowledgement is pending.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attempt_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.

### `propose_batch_item_payment`

Submit the amount of a batch item with an explicit bank version and idempotency key. A new key can create another payment; the caller must establish whether another submission is needed.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `bank_version` | integer | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `submission_key` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.

### `propose_batch_recipient_update`

Update the recipient version of one unpaid batch item from approved bank evidence. Does not cancel previously transmitted instructions.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `submission_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.

### `propose_batch_residual_payment`

Submit an explicit positive portion of a batch item principal with an immutable bank version and idempotency key. Aggregate supplier obligation limits remain the caller responsibility.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `item_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `bank_version` | integer | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `submission_key` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `amount_minor` | integer | yes | Use integer minor currency units derived from the current obligation and the published business rules. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
